item.content:encoded:
Lost amid the embarrassing madness of Tuesday's Wild Card series opener between the Boston Red Sox and the New York Yankees was Roman Anthony being pinch-hit for midway through the game, seemingly out of nowhere. After the game, it was revealed by manager Chad Tracy that Anthony had re-aggravated the wrist injury that had kept him out for more than three months during the regular season — and that his Game 2 status was up in the air.
Well, Boston's Game 2 lineup is out, and it's safe to say the fan base won't like it, with Anthony on the bench.
Is Roman Anthony playing tonight? Red Sox's lineup gives answer
Here's a look at Boston's Anthony-less lineup against Yankees left-hander Max Fried.
| Player | Position |
|---|---|
| 1. Jahmai Jones | DH |
| 2. Adley Rutschman | C |
| 3. Willson Contreras | 1B |
| 4. Wilyer Abreu | RF |
| 5. Ceddanne Rafaela | CF |
| 6. Caleb Durbin | 3B |
| 7. Nick Sogard | 2B |
| 8. Trevor Story | SS |
| 9. Nate Eaton | LF |
Yeah, the Red Sox are going to miss Anthony dearly. Sure, there's the makings of a decent lineup here. Jahmai Jones has done nothing but crush lefties since the Red Sox acquired him. Adley Rutschman and Willson Contreras are proven stars. Wilyer Abreu has broken out against left-handers this season, in particular. Ceddanne Rafaela is having his best offensive year. Still, there's no replacing Anthony.
He only appeared in 55 regular-season games and didn't look great in his two at-bats on Tuesday, but nobody in Boston's organization has a higher ceiling than Anthony. Being without him makes the already daunting challenge of rebounding from an 0-1 deficit in the best-of-three series that much more difficult.
Red Sox's growing injury report makes it tougher to believe in dream run
What makes Anthony's injury that much more difficult is that he's far from the only one. The Red Sox have a slew of notables on the IL, and that's making achieving their ultimate gol tough to believe in.
| Player | Position | Injury | Return |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mickey Gasper | C/INF | Right biceps strain | 2027 |
| Tyron Guerrero | RHP | Right shoulder strain | 2027 |
| Eli White | INF/OF | Ligament damage in right foot | 2027 |
| Curtis Mead | INF | Left wrist fracture | Postseason or 2027 |
| Kutter Crawford | RHP | Right flexor irritation | 2027 |
| Johan Oviedo | RHP | Right flexor strain | Postseason or 2027 |
| Anthony Siegler | INF | Right wrist discomfort | Postseason or 2027 |
| Justin Slaten | RHP | Right elbow inflammation | 2027 |
| Masataka Yoshida | DH | Left hamstring strain | Postseason or 2027 |
| Triston Casas | 1B | Left abdominal strain | 2027 |
The list is lengthy and littered with quality talent. Lineup-wise, the Red Sox sure could use Mickey Gasper, who was one of their hottest hitters before suffering his injury, right about now. They could also use Curtis Mead, a player who crushes left-handed pitching. Even Masataka Yoshida's bat would really come in handy with Anthony out.
Pitching-wise, Boston's depth has taken a hit. Tyron Guerrero and Justin Slaten are two of the most important members of their bullpen, and perhaps they would've been able to keep the game closer on Tuesday had they been healthy. Guys like Kutter Crawford and Johan Oviedo are proven back-end starters who could've eaten innings this October.
Perhaps the Red Sox can get Mead and a few others back if they can get past the Yankees, but with Anthony now joining the laundry list of injured players, it's getting tough to believe in them making a comeback.

item.content:encoded:
Roman Anthony's early exit is major cause for concern for Red Sox originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Red Sox hit some bumps in September, but their hope was that they would be the healthiest they have been all season by the time the postseason rolled around.
That's easier said than done. While Garrett Crochet is back and Boston's Game 1 lineup against the Yankees featured Roman Anthony, Willson Contreras and Ceddanne Rafaela, Contreras is believed to be playing at less than 100 percent — and Anthony is now dealing with an ailment of his own.
The young Red Sox outfielder exited Game 1 in the sixth inning, and manager Chad Tracy's postgame update was concerning to Boston fans.
Here's the latest on Anthony's status.
Roman Anthony exits Game 1
Anthony was pinch-hit for in the sixth inning of Game 1, a move that raised a few eyebrows. After the game, Tracy made it clear that it wasn't just a strategic decision,
Tracy told reporters that Anthony's hand, which forced him to miss most of the season, "flared" during the game. While Tracy said Anthony has felt occasional pain in his hand since returning, this instance was "more serious" and uncomfortable."
Chad Tracy said Roman Anthony had experienced the occasional "zinger" in that hand in the month since he returned.
"Today some stuff happened that was more serious and was uncomfortable," Tracy said. https://t.co/MkBoWPP4AD
Anthony previously winced after a check swing during the Red Sox' final game of the regular season, indicating he was dealing with some pain in the hand.
Here's what we know about Anthony's status for Game 2.
MORE: How Cam Schlittler became enemy No. 1 for Red Sox fans
Roman Anthony injury update
Anthony left Yankee Stadium before the Red Sox' postgame media availability and did not speak to reporters Tuesday night.
Asked directly whether Anthony would be available for Game 2, Tracy told reporters, "It's hard to say right now. It's one of those things where he obviously was in a lot of discomfort."
The Red Sox were shut out in Game 1, raising the level of urgency all-around in the clubhouse. Losing Anthony's bat would be a blow to Boston's lineup, though the former No. 1 prospect struggled down the stretch after a red-hot first week back from his months-long absence.

item.title: [BoSox Injection] Adley Rutschman justifies Red Sox trade with pre-playoff hot streak amid injuries and uncertainty
item.dc:creator: Katie Manganelli
item.description: The Boston Red Sox have not entered the postseason on a high note. The Sox's offense has seriously struggled in the lead up to the postseason, as well. Boston posted a league-worst .651 OPS and 71 runs scored in September — that's 18 fewer runs than the Philadelphia Phillies, the second-worst run scoring team in the season's final
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox have not entered the postseason on a high note. Not only are Willson Contreras and Ceddanne Rafaela not at 100 percent health-wise, Mickey Gasper, Eli White, Tyron Guerrero and other players are down with injuries.
The Sox's offense has seriously struggled in the lead up to the postseason, as well. Boston posted a league-worst .651 OPS and 71 runs scored in September — that's 18 fewer runs than the Philadelphia Phillies, the second-worst run scoring team in the season's final month.
But as the rest of his team has faltered, Adley Rutschman is heating up just at the right time. The former Baltimore Orioles catcher is slashing .266/.299/.547 in September, which might not seem like a huge breakout, but he batted just .170/.254/.245 in August, his first month in Boston.
Rutschman's last week is the most encouraging sign yet for the Sox. He's slashing .346/.370/.577 with a home run in his last seven games. Baseball is a game of momentum and Rutschman is one of the few Red Sox entering the Wild Card series hot. Boston will need his best work at the plate this series, especially from the right side, given the injuries it's dealing with. Thankfully, Rutschman is finally thriving from the right-handed batter's box.
Adley Rutschman is heating up for the Red Sox right at the perfect time
The Red Sox paid a hefty price for Rutschman at the trade deadline to bring a much-needed upgrade to their catcher spot. The 28-year-old is one of the best defensive catchers in the league and he effectively eliminates any advantage opposing teams have at the plate and on the base paths, a boost Connor Wong certainly doesn't bring on his start days. Now, Rutschman is finally starting to give the Sox the offensive production they hoped for when they sold all their best minor league pitchers and more for him.
Boston has rewarded Rutschman with the No. 2 spot in their Wild Card Game 1 lineup (subscription required). Manager Chad Tracy foreshadowed his placement in the lineup during the last game of the season against the Cubs, in which Rutschman went 1-for-2 with a homer and a walk. Batting him second is quite a risk, given the catcher's offensive trouble this season, but the Sox need all the help they can get at the plate and Rutschman is their hottest bat.
Rutschman doesn't have a ton of playoff experience from his tenure with the Orioles, but the five games he's played in October are more than many Sox players have under their belt. As one of their only players who's felt the pressure of the postseason on more than one occasion, the Red Sox need Rutschman to stay hot.

item.content:encoded:
After the Boston Red Sox went on their summer run to climb safely into an American League wild-card spot, that proved to be huge. Nobody can predict injuries, but it was a rough month of September in terms of injuries.
Not only did manager Chad Tracy lose Gold Glove outfielder Ceddanne Rafaela to an injury early in the month, but he also lost All-Star first baseman Willson Contreras to an injury with 10 days left in the regular season. Contreras was hit on the hand by a pitch against the Texas Rangers. He played in just one game after that.
He’ll be back in the Red Sox lineup for Game 1 of the AL wild-card series on Tuesday night against the New York Yankees. Boston is also getting Rafaela back in the Bronx, but the lineup will look different against Cam Schlittler.
Ceddanne Rafaela Batting Fifth in Game 1 vs. New York Yankees
Boston announced their lineup hours before Game 1 and Rafaela will be hitting fifth. Here is the lineup for the Red Sox,
Wilyer Abreu RF
Caddanne Rafaela CF
Nick Sogard 2B
Jarren Duran LF
Trevor Story SS
Caleb Durbin 3B
Rafaela was placed on the injured list with a right quadriceps strain, which caused him to miss 17 games. He returned against the Cleveland Guardians on Sept. 23 before exiting the game with right hamstring tightness while legging out a single. The next day, testing came back clean, and he was diagnosed with a hamstring cramp. He went 2-for-6 against the Guardians and Chicago Cubs in three games before the playoffs with a pair of singles.
Red Sox Big Wild Card Lead Led To Key Rest for Ceddanne Rafaela
If Rafaela can return and produce for Tracy, the big lead in the playoff race in the American League was huge. It allowed Boston to give not only Rafaela time to rest, but also Contreras as well.
Boston will be without utility infielder Mickey Gasper, who suffered an injury last Friday in Game 1 of a doubleheader against the Cubs at Fenway Park. He was placed on the 10-day injured list, which takes an underrated bat out of Tracy’s lineup and off his bench.
The Red Sox will send young left-hander Payton Tolle to the mound against the New York Yankees, who will send this lineup out for manager Aaron Boone,
Ben Rice DH
Heliot Ramos RF
George Lombard Jr. SS
Amed Rosario 3B
Anthony Vole 2B
New York won’t have Aaron Judge for the series, as he was not part of Boone’s roster. This figures to be a low-scoring series given the projected pitching matchups for the three games, if it goes that far. Boston getting Rafaela and Contreras back while the Yankees not having Judge feels like an advantage for the Red Sox. Winning Game 1 is big in a best-of-three series, especially for the Yankees, with Boston having Sonny Gray scheduled to go in Game 2 on Wednesday night.

item.title: [si.com] The Potentially Fatal Flaw For Each MLB Playoff Team
item.dc:creator: Ryan Phillips
item.description: The MLB playoffs are here as 12 teams survived the regular season and are ready for an all-out battle for October supremacy. Each of the remaining squads has spent the last six months proving it belonged in the postseason. None of the last teams standing got here unscathed and all have glaring weaknesses that could end their seasons early. With postseason baseball upon us, here is the fatal flaw that could derail each MLB playoff team. Brewers: Lack of Power The Brewers were baseball’s best team
item.content:encoded:
The MLB playoffs are here as 12 teams survived the regular season and are ready for an all-out battle for October supremacy. Each of the remaining squads has spent the last six months proving it belonged in the postseason. None of the last teams standing got here unscathed and all have glaring weaknesses that could end their seasons early.
With postseason baseball upon us, here is the fatal flaw that could derail each MLB playoff team.
Brewers: Lack of Power
The Brewers were baseball’s best team all season but that doesn’t mean they’re perfect. Milwaukee has a great rotation fronted by baseball’s new ace Jacob Misiorowski, and a good bullpen, but the lineup relies heavily on getting hits up and down the lineup. The Brewers play the 2026 version of small ball, and don’t have a ton of power. That can kill teams in October, when runs come at a premium.
Milwaukee finished the season tied for 28th in home runs (154) and 25th in isolated power (.144). The Brewers were tied for 10th in slugging (.403) and were third in wRC+ (107), but the lack of top-line power could be their downfall. Against elite pitching in the postseason, it’s much more difficult to string together hits and build big innings. Being able to get runs on balls that leave the yard is huge. Each of the last six World Series champions ranked inside the top five in regular season home runs.
Maybe Milwaukee bucks that trend, but if they don’t win the World Series, a lack of power may be the reason.
Dodgers: Health
The Dodgers have won two straight titles and at full strength, they’d be the overwhelming favorite to take home a third in a row. But L.A. has dealt with major injuries all season and the team looks more vulnerable than it has in a long time as we enter the postseason.
Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow combined to make only 22 starts this season. Both are back now, but neither has been particularly reliable—Snell left his penultimate start on Sept. 16 with a groin injury before returning to pitch four innings on Saturday. Tarik Skubal had elbow surgery earlier this year with the Tigers and hasn’t been quite as dominant as usual when it comes to limiting baserunners. Shohei Ohtani has been sidelined by knee and biceps injuries, and won’t be pitching in October. Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts and Teoscar Hernandez are showing signs of decline and have played a ton of baseball over the last three years.
L.A. is still loaded, but a few injuries to a roster that’s had its fair share of medical issues could make things dicey.
Rays: Trouble Against Lefties
It’s hard to find too many flaws here. The Rays are an incredibly balanced squad that was the best in the AL pretty much all season. One of the only red flags here is the team’s performance against lefties, and they’re likely to run into a few in the playoffs.
Against lefties as a team, Tampa Bay ranked 27th in slugging (.364), 26th in wRC+ (90) and 25th in OPS (.679). Luckily for the Rays, their best offensive players hammered lefties. Junior Caminero slashed .287/.426/.490 with eight home runs and a 152 wRC+. Unfortunately, the 23-year-old and Yandy Diaz are the team’s only players who appeared in 100-plus games and topped .700 in OPS against lefties.
That’s a weakness opponents will try to exploit in October. The Rays don’t have many holes, but good left-handed pitching could be the kryptonite that slows one of baseball’s most complete teams.
Braves: A Hole at Shortstop
The Braves have plenty of star power in the lineup and Chris Sale at the top of their rotation but they have a huge flaw at the heart of their team. Atlanta’s shortstops were among the worst offensively during the 2026 season. Ha-seong Kim is is the starter, but he had a .359 OPS with zero home runs in 147 plate appearances this season so I’m not sure that is the answer. The other option is Mauricio Dubón, who had a .719 OPS in 153 games, but that won’t work against southpaws since it means lefty Mike Yastrzemski must play left field.
Collectively, Braves shortstops slashed .241/.295/.349 during the regular season and ranked 27th with a wRC+ of 78. They also ranked 23rd in fWAR (1.6) and bWAR (-0.4). They simply haven’t gotten enough out of the position and need to find some offensive production there.
Atlanta went wire-to-wire to win the NL East and did so while not getting much from a premium position. Against elite pitching in the postseason, they’ll need production out of everyone in the lineup at some point. Carrying an empty spot will likely prove to be more damaging than it already has been.
Yankees: An Aaron Judge-Sized Hole in the Lineup
The Yankees may have baseball’s best postseason rotation and found enough offense to hold onto the AL’s top wild-card spot. But to win a World Series, they need their best player healthy and hammering baseballs. They may not have it.
Aaron Judge is trying to return for the wild-card series from a strained calf muscle, but it would be unwise to rush him back into action. Yes, New York needs his bat in the lineup, but it also needs to ensure he is available for the entire postseason, not just the first series. Ben Rice (149), Cody Bellinger (115) and Paul Goldschmidt (111) are the only Yankees with more than 300 plate appearances and a wRC+ over 100. That’s a scary lack of production from the lineup.
They need Judge’s bat back at full health as soon as possible simply because the team relies on him so much to produce.
Padres: Who Starts After Michael King?
The Padres have baseball’s best bullpen and an offense that has been clicking on all cylinders in the second half. What they don’t have is a deep rotation after injuries have decimated it.
Michael King is the team’s ace and should be reliable in that spot, but after him things get dicey. Nick Pivetta missed most of the season due to a flexor strain in his pitching elbow that cost him nearly five months. He’s back and has thrown well, but he’s only made eight starts this year. After that, it’ll be some combination of Robbie Ray and Walker Buehler. Both have been up and down this season and neither feels like a rock-solid option.
If San Diego can get decent starts and shorten games by getting the bullpen in early, things could be fine. But if the team’s starters struggle it could mean an early exit.
Cubs: A Battered Starting Rotation
The Cubs have one of baseball’s best offenses and its best all-around player in Pete Crow-Armstrong, but their pitching staff remains a patchwork mess. The team’s starting rotation has endured season-ending injuries to Cade Horton and Ben Brown, Justin Steele still hasn’t returned after elbow surgery in 2025, Matthew Boyd missed time thanks to knee surgery and a shoulder issue, and Kevin Gausman is now dealing with a shoulder injury.
Chicago will open the postseason with Boyd on the mound and should follow with Clay Holmes in Game 2, then Shota Imanaga and, if he’s healthy enough, Gausman. How bad has it been for the Cubs? Among starters, only Imanaga generated 2.0 bWAR this year. That’s a dangerous weakness to carry into the postseason when pitching becomes even more important.
Could the Cubs manage to overcome a rotation that has been battered all season? It’s possible, but that would take a herculean effort from the team’s top-ranked offense.
Phillies: Trea Turner’s Disappearing Production
Trea Turner was a key piece of the Phillies’ success in 2025, as he slashed .302/.354/.450 with 15 home runs, 36 stolen bases and a 123 wRC+ in 141 games. The team is probably wondering where that guy went.
In 157 games this year, Turner slashed .242/.297/.378 with 19 home runs, 21 stolen bases and a wRC+ of 83. His strikeout rate jumped from 16.7% to 21.0%, his xBA dropped from .270 to .242 and his xwOBA of .293 ranked in the 14th percentile. That would be manageable if Turner provided value defensively, but his outs above average dropped from 17 in 2025 to -8 this season. That’s a precipitous, ominous drop for a shortstop who’s in his age-33 season, has always depended on his athleticism and still has seven more years on his contract. Philadelphia has underachieved as a whole in 2026, and Turner is the poster child.
While he was a disappointment in the regular season, Turner has a ton of playoff experience and won a title with the Nationals in 2019. Maybe he’ll turn it around when the lights are the brightest. But his postseason track record doesn’t offer much optimism. He has a career playoff OPS of .681.
Red Sox: A Top-Heavy Offense
Boston’s comeback story this season was remarkable after Alex Cora was fired following a 10–17 start. While they were one of MLB’s best teams over the final two-thirds of the season, the offense never really clicked one through nine. As a team, the Red Sox finished 17th in wRC+ (99) and 19th in OPS (.717). And it seemed all season a few guys would come through, while the rest of the lineup struggled.
Among the team’s hitters who played at least 100 games, only Willson Contreras (151), Wilyer Abreu (112) and Ceddanne Rafaela (109) topped 100 in wRC+ to grade out as above-average hitters. The drop-off from Contreras to the rest of the roster is pretty alarming in itself, though Mickey Gasper (130), Masataka Yoshida (108) and Roman Anthony (106) all performed well in fewer than 300 plate appearances. Key pieces like Caleb Durbin (100) and especially Jarren Duran (69) had off years, while catcher Adley Rutschman slashed .222/.278/.410 with a wRC+ of 88 after arriving at the trade deadline.
Boston will have to overcome those issues throughout the lineup, particularly against the kind of pitching ahead in the postseason. The lack of offensive balance could be the team’s downfall.
Guardians: A Lineup Short of Firepower
The Guardians are in an enviable position, as they barely made the playoffs but wound up with the AL’s No. 2 seed. While they are set up for success thanks to the bracket and have an excellent pitching staff, their lineup has been anemic.
Cleveland finished the regular season ranked 27th in home runs (162) and slugging (.380), 26th in OPS (.696), 24th in runs scored (678) and 21st in wRC+ (97). Meanwhile, star third baseman José Ramírez wrapped up the worst full season of his career, slashing .235/.320/.368 with 12 home runs and a wRC+ of 92. The question is simple: Where do the runs come from? Rookie Chase DeLauter was the team’s most productive hitter after slashing .287/.363/.456 with 16 home runs and a 131 wRC+, but he doesn't have much help. Steven Kwan was second on the team in wRC+ (114), but only slugged .349, while Travis Bazzana (110) and Angel Martinez (108) were both only modestly above average by wRC+. The rest of the lineup struggled to generate offense.
After a tough battle down the stretch, the Guardians wound up with a favorable path in the postseason. But getting to the World Series will likely require unearthing some unsung heroes on offense.
White Sox: October Inexperience
The White Sox surprised everyone with their run to a postseason berth after three consecutive 100-loss seasons. The roster has been properly overhauled, with only 19.8% of the team’s plate appearances coming from players on the 121-loss team in 2024. The problem is, most of the team’s new players have little to no postseason experience.
Braden Montgomery, Munetaka Murakami and Sam Antonacci are rookies, while Colson Montgomery, Kyle Teel, Chase Meidroth and Grant Taylor are second-year players. Sean Burke debuted in 2024, but has never pitched in the postseason, and All-Star Miguel Vargas has likewise never appeared in the postseason despite coming up with the Dodgers. Maybe there’s something to be said for youthful exuberance, but there’s also the possibility that fatigue becomes a factor for players who haven’t been through a playoff chase before. Colson Montgomery posted a wRC+ of 54 after August 1, while Murakami slashed .156/.299/.375 in that stretch.
Chicago is built for success long-term, but its lack of postseason experience could be a significant obstacle in October.
Astros: A Thin Starting Rotation
The Astros finished 81–81 to win the weak AL West and notch a playoff spot. Given their record, it’s not surprising they have a ton of issues across the roster. The most glaring is their starting rotation, which is in rough shape.
Beyond Hunter Brown, Houston simply doesn’t have the kind of high-end starting pitching that wins in October. And even Brown enters the playoffs with some uncertainty, having thrown only 107 ⅓ innings this season after missing a chunk of the campaign with a shoulder injury. Peter Lambert has become the team’s No. 2 starter, but he went 8–10 with a 3.82 ERA and doesn’t possess premium stuff. Hayden Wesneski finished the season strong, but made only 11 starts all year, while Cristian Javier and Mike Burrows are both on the IL.
The rotation is so thin that the Astros are poised to open Game 1 of the wild-card series with a bullpen game to give Brown, Lambert and Wesneski rest. It’s hardly an ideal situation and there aren’t many options available for manager Joe Espada.
Ryan Phillips is a senior writer on the Breaking and Trending News team at Sports Illustrated. He has worked in digital media since 2009, spending eight years at The Big Lead before joining SI in 2024. Phillips also co-hosts The Assembly Call Podcast about Indiana Hoosiers basketball and previously worked at Bleacher Report. He is a proud San Diego native and a graduate of Indiana University’s journalism program.

item.title: [Over the Monster] Chad Tracy could swing the series between the Red Sox and Yankees
item.dc:creator: Keagan Stiefel
item.description: Chad Tracy is hardly the only person that has been added to the fold between the Boston Red Sox and New York Yankees’ back-to-back meetings in the American League Wild Card Series. The Red Sox have made substantial additions to the rotation, with Payton Tolle, Sonny Gray, and Ranger Suarez being named the starting pitchers for the best-of-three series at Yankee Stadium — making for a much deeper unit than the one that fell off a cliff after Garrett Crochet last season and relied on the likes of
item.content:encoded:
Chad Tracy is hardly the only person that has been added to the fold between the Boston Red Sox and New York Yankees’ back-to-back meetings in the American League Wild Card Series.
The Red Sox have made substantial additions to the rotation, with Payton Tolle, Sonny Gray, and Ranger Suarez being named the starting pitchers for the best-of-three series at Yankee Stadium — making for a much deeper unit than the one that fell off a cliff after Garrett Crochet last season and relied on the likes of Brayan Bello and Connelly Early. Roman Anthony, Willson Contreras, Adley Rutschman, and Caleb Durbin will join the lineup in hopes to scrape together more than the six total runs they scored last season. Crochet could end up joining the bullpen in his return from injury, along with newcomers Erik Miller and Jake Bennett, which is a pretty decent group of pitchers being added to one of the very best units in baseball this season.
The Yankees will also be in a better position on the pitching side, with Gerrit Cole serving as the do-or-die option behind Cam Schlittler and Max Fried. Luis Garcia Jr., Heliot Ramos, and George Lombard Jr. should help the lineup against left-handers, though there is something to be said about the so-so status of Aaron Judge.
If we can boil all of that down, though, only one man can completely swing the series…
Chad Tracy.
Tracy’s most difficult decisions might come before the season even starts, as he will be relied upon heavily to figure out who will fill out the roster — Braiden Ward? Jarren Duran? Curtis Mead? Jahmai Jones? Nate Eaton? Isiah Kiner-Falefa? Crochet?
It’s not going to be easy, but all of that pales in comparison to making decisions with who will play, when they will play, and how he manages things when the lights are at their brightest in The Bronx.
“It’s the playoffs, so we’re at the point in the season where teams that are remaining need to win or they’re going home,” Tracy said during his media availability on Monday. “I have a feel for that.
“… It’s all hands on deck. I think everyone is aware that during the playoffs it’s about winning moments and being aggressive — all those things. I think most of our guys who have been around understand that, so we’re going to go out and play our butts off and manage and do everything we can to win each game.”
Alex Cora, the manager of last year’s squad that became the first in history to lose the best-of-three series after taking a lead, made some… interesting decisions in hindsight.
Bello was pulled after 2 1/3 innings in Game 2, which led to Justin Wilson, Zack Kelly, Garrett Whitlock, and Tolle being used out of the bullpen and becoming unavailable for Game 3. Nate Eaton started over Wilyer Abreu in Game 2. Rob Refsnyder got two starts over Masataka Yoshida, which makes sense considering they faced two left-handers, but he finished 0-for-5 while the latter went 4-for-7. Nathaniel Lowe played in all three games, while Nick Sogard only played in two.
It’s easy to go back in time and poke holes though these decisions with the benefit of hindsight, but that’s kind of the whole point in looking ahead at the same two teams playing each other again with one of them being led by someone new.
Tracy needs to avoid making similar mistakes, and he needs to do it without the benefit of years of experience in similar situations. The Red Sox stripped him of that interim tag because they believe he can, and it’s only a matter of time before we find out whether or not they’re right.

item.dc:creator: Zach Coe

item.content:encoded:
RedSoxRoundtable's Zach Coe discusses some roster decisions to keep an eye on ahead of the postseason rosters finalizing on the 'Entering Kenmore' Podcast. Subscribe on YouTube and be sure to join our FREE community over on RedSoxRoundtable.com!
The Boston Red Sox have arrived in New York ahead of their Wild Card series against the New York Yankees, which begins Tuesday night (8:00 p.m. ET). Before taking the field to determine who advances to a divisional-round series against the Tampa Bay Rays, both teams were made available to the media Monday afternoon at Yankee Stadium.
Here's what you need to know about Red Sox manager Chad Tracy's media availability:
Payton Tolle further cements his status as a budding ace
The big story of Tracy's availability was the announcement of the starting rotation for the series, headlined by 23-year-old rookie Payton Tolle taking the mound in Tuesday's Game 1. Tolle has already established himself as one of baseball's best young arms, putting together a rookie campaign that should see him finish in the top three in American League Rookie of the Year voting.
Even with Tolle's regular-season success, few, if any, other 23-year-old rookies would be trusted to take the mound in Game 1 of a postseason series in an environment as hostile as Yankee Stadium.
"Just felt like with his power stuff that was the best choice for Game 1," Tracy said of the decision to start Tolle. "I know his age; I know he's a rookie, but as far as he approaches baseball and big moments, that part won't bother him. He's a pretty special personality... he's just going to go out there and pitch his game regardless of what it is," he continued.
Tolle has earned the trust and respect of his teammates and coaching staff, and they feel confident in his ability to go head-to-head with the likely American League Cy Young Award winner, Yankees starter Cam Schlittler, which is a real testament to his future as the Red Sox' ace.
Garrett Crochet's status remains up in the air
Speaking of Cy Young-caliber pitchers, the 2025 AL Cy Young runner-up Garrett Crochet traveled with the team to New York after throwing a live bullpen in Ft. Myers on Saturday. Despite being with the team, Crochet's status for the Wild Card round remains up in the air as the team continues to monitor his left shoulder's recovery after each day of work.
In order to activate Crochet, the Red Sox brass will have several questions they'll need to answer: most importantly, how many games would Crochet be available to pitch in? While an arm like Crochet's in the bullpen could be a massive weapon for Tracy, if he can only pitch once in the three-game set, would the roster spot be better served by a pitcher who can give you multiple appearances?
"If we're able to activate [Crochet], obviously he's available, right? But I think beyond that, if we were to use him, the availability- whether that be the next day- would still be contingent on us continuing to evaluate him," Tracy said of Crochet's potential availability.
With Tyron Guerrero injured and out for at least the first two rounds of the postseason, creating a major hole in the back end of the Boston bullpen, it would be a relative surprise to see Crochet not on the Wild Card roster.
Willson Contreras will return to first base
After a pitch hit him in the hand in Boston's 4-3 win over the Texas Rangers on Sept. 17, Red Sox All-Star first baseman Willson Contreras cast doubt on his postseason availability after Thursday's series finale against the Cleveland Guardians. However, the 34-year-old returned to the lineup for Sunday's regular-season finale against the Chicago Cubs, logging two at-bats as the designated hitter.
Tracy told reporters that Contreras' inclusion in the lineup as DH was simply to give him some live reps in a game and that, as long as he checks out well after Monday's workouts, the plan was for him to return to first base Tuesday night.
Braiden Ward remains an option to make the roster
One of the Red Sox' most underrated moves made ahead of the trade deadline was an under-the-radar deal made with the Atlanta Braves to acquire outfielder Eli White. The 32-year-old was set to serve a crucial role on the postseason roster as the fourth outfielder and pinch-running specialist. However, those plans were cut short when White sustained a torn ligament in his right foot on Sept. 8, requiring surgery that ended his season.
As a result of White's injury, the door opened for spring-training standout Braiden Ward, who set a Triple-A club record for most stolen bases in a single season, to join the club for his big-league debut as a base-running specialist.
The 27-year-old is with the club in New York, but Tracy cautioned reporters not to read too much into his presence, as the roster is still being worked through.
Up next for the Sox
After weeks of discussion about what felt like an inevitable postseason matchup, the two rivals will take the field at Yankee Stadium on Tuesday night to kick off the best-of-three series. Tolle (9-6, 3.03 ERA) gets the start for Boston opposite Schlittler (14-6, 1.95 ERA) for New York. First pitch is set for 8:00 p.m. ET.
For more on the Wild Card series
Zach Coe and David Azer are back on the 'Entering Kenmore' Podcast, previewing the Red Sox' Wild Card matchup with the Yankees. Check it out wherever you get your podcasts or in the YouTube player below.

item.title: [mlb.com] Willson returns to lineup, should play in WC Series; Gasper, Guerrero placed on IL
item.dc:creator: Joey Johnston
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG — After missing eight games, Willson Contreras returned to the Red Sox’s lineup, batting third and serving as designated hitter in Boston’s 6-2 loss to the Cubs in Sunday’s regular-season finale at Tropicana Field. Red Sox manager Chad Tracy indicated that Contreras, who was hit on the right hand by a pitch on Sept. 17 at Texas, will be active for the American League Wild Card Series, which begins Tuesday night at Yankee Stadium. “He should be [good to go],’’ Tracy said. Game 162
item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG — After missing eight games, Willson Contreras returned to the Red Sox’s lineup, batting third and serving as designated hitter in Boston’s 6-2 loss to the Cubs in Sunday’s regular-season finale at Tropicana Field.
Red Sox manager Chad Tracy indicated that Contreras, who was hit on the right hand by a pitch on Sept. 17 at Texas, will be active for the American League Wild Card Series, which begins Tuesday night at Yankee Stadium.
“He should be [good to go],’’ Tracy said.
Game 162 was moved from Boston’s Fenway Park to the Trop, home of the Tampa Bay Rays, as a precaution when a weekend nor’easter battered the East Coast with torrential rain and heavy winds. Contreras went 0-for-2 with a strikeout and a groundout before being lifted for pinch-hitter Jahmai Jones in the fifth.
The return of Contreras, who was batting .276 with 27 home runs and 81 RBIs before his injury, was greeted enthusiastically by Tracy and his Red Sox teammates.
“Huge … massive," Tracy said of Contreras’ potential postseason availability. “Even with a layoff, with a guy like that, you know what he’s capable of doing with one swing of the bat. It’s pretty well documented. That’s so much what the postseason is about, these big moments where one swing can change a game. So that power and that presence in the middle of the order is important."
Tracy said Contreras made “pretty significant" improvement and looked impressive in batting practice Saturday, when the Red Sox conducted an optional workout at the Trop during an off-day.
“That was a huge step," Tracy said. “So we’ll get him some live at-bats in a game, and hopefully we’re good to go."
Third baseman Caleb Durbin said Contreras’ return provided energy in the Red Sox clubhouse.
“We’ve been without Willson and Rafa [Ceddanne Rafaela, who missed 17 games with a right quad strain] for a while," Durbin said. “We know what having those guys in the postseason could mean. We’re a different team [with them].
“I think we all feed off [Contreras’] energy. Just having him around and activated is big for us. He’s a big leader. Having that type of experience and energy, with him laying it on the line every single time he’s out there, it will add a lot to the playoff environment. We’re excited to have them back for this level of meaningful baseball."
Along with Contreras’ return, the Red Sox lost a couple of key performers to the injured list. Catcher/first baseman Mickey Gasper was placed on the 10-day IL with a right biceps strain, while right-handed reliever Tyron Guerrero was placed on the 15-day IL with a right shoulder strain.
Gasper batted .251 with 10 homers, 24 RBIs and an .823 OPS in 67 games. Guerrero (a 3.10 ERA in 40 appearances) already had missed most of September because of shoulder inflammation.
The Red Sox recalled infielder/outfielder Nate Eaton and right-handed pitcher Wyatt Olds. Tracy said the organization is still debating how to structure Boston’s postseason roster, but he added that Eaton brings value as an extra outfielder because of his speed and defense.
Another option could be ace left-hander Garrett Crochet, who hasn’t pitched for the Red Sox since April 25 but could return as a reliever. Tracy said Crochet did well during Saturday’s live batting practice session in Fort Myers, Fla. Crochet will likely join Boston in New York, but it’s not yet certain he will be on the postseason roster.

item.title: [sbnation.com] MLB Playoffs: Ranking all 12 teams by their World Series 2026 chances
item.dc:creator: Mark Schofield
item.description: The MLB postseason is here. There are 12 teams headed to the playoffs including the Houston Astros and the Philadelphia Phillies, who needed wins in Game 162 to punch their respective tickets to the dance. But now, records reset to 0-0, and all 12 teams have an equal chance to win the World Series. At least in theory. But some teams are in a better position than others as the playoffs beckon. item.content:encoded:
The MLB postseason is here.
There are 12 teams headed to the playoffs including the Houston Astros and the Philadelphia Phillies, who needed wins in Game 162 to punch their respective tickets to the dance. But now, records reset to 0-0, and all 12 teams have an equal chance to win the World Series.
At least in theory.
But some teams are in a better position than others as the playoffs beckon. Here are the 12 teams in the MLB Playoffs, ranked by their chances of winning the World Series.
12. Houston Astros (81-81)
The Houston Astros became the first team in MLB history to win the division without a winning record.
This is a team that can mash, as the Astros led the majors with 226 home runs, 42 off the bat of MVP candidate Yordan Alvarez. Four other members of the lineup topped 20 home runs as well: Christian Walker, Jeremy Peña, Isaac Paredes, and Cam Smith.
But the problem is pitching, as the Astros were 24th in MLB in ERA and 21st in WHIP. Closer Josh Hader was solid in the second half, racking up 16 saves and posting a WHIP of 0.682, and Bryan Abreu has been dependable in front of him, but the bullpen has been inconsistent beyond those two.
So if the rotation cannot pitch deep into games, that will be a problem.
11. Chicago White Sox (84-78)
After losing more than 100 games in each of the past three seasons, the Chicago White Sox were one of baseball’s best stories this year, leading the AL Central for much of the season before sliding into the playoffs with a Wild Card spot.
Chicago is powered by a lineup that features three players with more than 30 home runs — Munetaka Murakami, Colson Montgomery, and Miguel Vargas — and as a team the White Sox posted an OBP 0f .320, second only to the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League.
However, the problem in the playoffs might be starting pitching. As a staff the White Sox starting pitchers posted an ERA of 4.60 this season (26th in the majors) and a WHIP of 1.34 (25th in the majors). That sets up a tough matchup, starting with the Wild Card Series against Houston.
But, they do have the Pope on their side.
10. Philadelphia Phillies (88-74)
The Philadelphia Phillies cut their magic number for a playoff spot to one with a win over the Milwaukee Brewers last Tuesday.
They lost their next four games by a combined score of 23-3, needing a win on the final day of the season to book a postseason berth.
Philadelphia did that on Sunday, clinching the final Wild Card spot in the NL with a 7-3 win over the Tampa Bay Rays, and this star-laden team now gets a series with the Atlanta Braves to prove everyone wrong. Kyle Schwarber, Bryce Harper, and Trae Turner bring the star power, and Jhoan Duran remains one of the best closers in baseball. Philadelphia also has Zack Wheeler and Cristopher Sánchez leading the rotation; however, manager Don Mattingly was forced to use Sánchez in the season finale, complicating his availability this week. Then there is Aaron Nola, who is coming off a spot start on short rest on Saturday and needs to play a big role despite some struggles this season.
Can a weary rotation, and a bullpen that has endured its own share of struggles in front of Duran, get the job done? That is the big question.
9. Cleveland Guardians (85-77)
While the Chicago White Sox were one of the biggest surprises of the MLB season, in the end the Cleveland Guardians clinched the AL Central, and a first-round playoff bye.
Their reward? After the bye Cleveland will have home-field advantage against the winner of the Houston-Chicago series, and they will avoid any of the AL East teams until a potential ALCS matchup.
The Guardians are led by their pitching, as Cleveland boasts both a strong rotation and a stellar bullpen. Gavin Williams and Parker Messick pace a starting staff that produced the ninth-best ERA among starters and the bullpen, led by closer Cade Smith and the trio of setup arms Hunter Gaddis, Eric Sabrowski, and Tim Herrin was even better, with the sixth-best ERA among bullpens in the majors.
If Cleveland gets enough production from the offense, that pitching staff could power them to the ALCS, where anything can happen.
8. Boston Red Sox (87-75)
After a brutal start cost manager Alex Cora his job, the Boston Red Sox used a 32-5 stretch to push into playoff contention.
But Boston cooled off after that torrid summer, and there are some questions facing this team as the playoffs loom. One is the health of the lineup. Ceddanne Rafaela is back after missing 16 games with a quad injury, but will Willson Contreras be fully healthy after getting hit by a pitch on his right hand in the final week of the season? A second question? Can the lineup bounce back after a difficult September. As a team, Boston posted an OPS of .651 in the month of September.
Pitching is not a question. The trio of Payton Tolle, Sonny Gray, and Ranger Suárez is one of the best left standing, and Aroldis Chapman has been dynamic at the back of the bullpen yet again. Boston could even get Garrett Crochet back from injury in a relief role, and Tanner Houck — who started Game 162 more than 500 days after his last MLB appearance, after working back from Tommy John surgery — could be in the mix out of the bullpen as well.
Which version of the Red Sox shows up, however, is the ultimate question.
7. Chicago Cubs (89-73)
The Chicago Cubs have one of the best offenses in baseball, led by MVP candidate Pete Crow-Armstrong, the first center fielder in MLB history to produce a 40/40 season. This is a lineup that led the majors with a team OPS of .767, and a team slugging percentage of .428. Beyond Crow-Armstrong, Alex Bregman, Ian Happ, Michael Busch, and Seiya Suzuki all put 20 home runs on the board this season.
The Cubs also have one of the best defenses in baseball, again with Crow-Armstrong leading the way. The outfielder posted a Fielding Run Value (FRV) of +26 this season, tops in the majors, and the Cubs led all teams with a FRV of +72 this year, ahead of the St. Louis Cardinals who posted a +45.
The problem? Pitching. The Cubs starters posted a team ERA of 4.27 this year — worst among NL playoff teams — and only two teams gave up more home runs than the Cubs this year. And a staff that has been hampered by injuries faces another question on that front as the playoffs loom, as Kevin Gausman was injured on a tag play last week and suffered an injury to his non-throwing shoulder. Craig Counsell would love to have him for the series against the San Diego Padres.
The Cubs have the offense and the defense to win games, but do they have the pitching to win a series or two?
6. San Diego Padres (91-71)
If momentum could be measured, the San Diego Padres might be off the charts.
The Padres went 17-11 in August, and then 18-6 in September, to lock down a Wild Card spot. This was quite the turnaround for a team that was flirting with being sellers at the trade deadline. Leading the way was outfielder Fernando Tatis Jr., who did not homer over the first 55 games of the season but finished with 25 home runs and 38 steals, thanks to a torrid closing stretch. Jackson Merrill overcame a slow start of his own to finish with 26 home runs and 27 steals, giving the Padres their first 25/25 duo.
As a lineup, the Padres were second in both OPS and slugging percentage after the All-Star break, behind only the Cubs.
San Diego also has one of the best bullpens in baseball, with closer Mason Miller in form behind setup men Adrian Morejon and Bradgley Rodriguez.
They’ll host the Cubs in the Wild Card Series, and while Chicago won the season series 5-1, that was before San Diego’s late-season turnaround.
5. New York Yankees (93-68)
When the New York Yankees lost Aaron Judge for an extended period of the regular season, the lineup stepped up in his absence. While Judge played just 66 games and hit 18 home runs, the Yankees managed to belt 223 home runs, finishing second in the majors.
But with his status in question for the Wild Card Series against Boston, the rest of that lineup will need to step up yet again. And the matchup against the Red Sox will be a tough one, as Boston will likely throw Payton Tolle, Sonny Gray, and Ranger Suárez against them — a strong start — and the Red Sox have one of the best bullpens in the game.
And that matchup will be even tougher without Judge’s bat in the lineup.
4. Atlanta Braves (94-67)
While the Atlanta Braves would have loved a first-round bye, with the Los Angeles Dodgers and the Milwaukee Brewers out of striking distance Atlanta was able to set their rotation for the Wild Card Series over the final week of the season. Chris Sale made his final start of the regular season last Wednesday on extra rest, and will be on extra rest when he gets the ball for Game 1. The same goes for Tyler Mahle, who will have extra rest ahead of an anticipated Game 2 start.
Plus the Braves get the Philadelphia Phillies in the Wild Card Series, who gave their fans something to worry about over the final few days of the season as they did not clinch a spot until Game 162.
3. Tampa Bay Rays (98-64)
Few people gave the Tampa Bay Rays a chance when the season began.
Leading with me, who put the Rays in the “True Longshots” category when the year began, along with the Diamondbacks, the Athletics, and the Twins.
But here are the Rays, the winners of the AL East and the team to beat in the American League. MCP candidate Junior Caminero has put up massive numbers for Tampa Bay — he slashed .276/.360/.524 this year along with 42 home runs — and is at the heart of a lineup that punishes pitchers from top-to-bottom. As a team the Rays hit .258 this season, the best number in the AL and tied with the Brewers for the top number in the majors, and the Rays also posted a team OPS of .728, behind only the Houston Astros in the American League.
Add in a staff that posted an MLB-best team WHIP of 1.14, tied with the Dodgers, and you have the recipe for a deep playoff run.
2. Los Angeles Dodgers (100-62)
The Los Angeles Dodgers got off to their annual hot start, endured a mid-season slump that raised more questions than answers about their chances at a three-peat, but enter the playoffs having found some of those answers.
Kyle Tucker’s season-long slump seems to be ending just in time for a post-season run, as he slashed .266/362/.557 in the month of September, his best stretch of the season by far. Shohei Ohtani and Will Smith are both back in the lineup, Edwin Diaz seems to have found his stuff — he was flawless in September, allowing just one hit in four appearances and striking out eight — and Mookie Betts is back to being Mookie Betts, as he slashed .345/.447/.690 in September, also putting up his best numbers of the season.
When you’ve won a pair of titles, you know when to turn it on.
The Dodgers seem to have done just that over the last month.
1. Milwaukee Brewers (103-59)
The Milwaukee Brewers top these rankings, as they topped 100 wins for the first time in franchise history.
But for this team, the real test comes in October. The Brewers have now won the NL Central for four consecutive years, and in five of the last six campaigns. What do they have to show for that? Two playoff wins, including a sweep at the hands of the Dodgers in the NLCS a year ago.
Jacob Misiorowski gives them a bonafide ace, as the big right-hander led the majors in ERA (1.86), ERA+ (225), WHIP (0.803), and K/9 (13.1) this season, and Logan Henderson has developed into a solid No. 2 for Milwaukee. If Kyle Harrison somehow recovers his first-half form (he was 8-2 with a 3.01 ERA before the All-Star Break, but went 3-3 with a 7.31 ERA in the second half of the season) this team could finally break through to the promised land.

Throughout the season, first baseman Willson Contreras has been the emotional heart for the Boston Red Sox. However, he largely hasn’t been able to play in the month of September due to injuries.
He spent time on the IL due to a hamstring injury. That had been bugging him for some time, and the Red Sox wanted him to reset and get healthy for the postseason. He did, but almost as soon as he came back, he was hit in the right hand by a pitch. That forced Contreras to miss about a week and a half before DHing in the final game of the season on Sunday.
Boston Red Sox Manager Chad Tracy on Willson Contreras in the Playoffs
In the end, Willson Contreras had just two at-bats on Sunday. He’d go 0-2 with a strikeout before Jahmai Jones came in to pinch-hit for him.
It was a small sample size, but it was another emotional boost that Contreras could provide the Red Sox. The postseason is here and he’s healthy enough to play. Better than that, after the game, Red Sox manager Chad Tracy confirmed that he should be available for the Wild Card Round in the postseason.
“He was okay,” Tracy said. “Took the first one [at-bat]. Took the second one. Had a pretty good at-bat. Hit the ball hard to third and he was good. So, I got him out of there… Should be [good to go].
Getting hit on the hand is risky, with plenty of smaller bones to break. Luckily, X-Rays showed that Contreras avoided that, and was just dealing with bad swelling that made it hard to swing a bat. He had previously been anxious about his availability for the postseason when describing it as a bone bruise.
“Yeah, there’s no fracture or anything,” Contreras said. “I had a CT scan yesterday just to make sure that I don’t have any fracture, and it didn’t show any fracture. At this point, still inflammation and a bone bruise.”
This comes at a time when the Red Sox have been desperately trying to get healthy. Players like Adley Rutschman and Caleb Durbin are banged up but playing through it. Others, like Ceddanne Rafaela and Curtis Mead, have needed to spend time on the IL.
Now, the Red Sox will turn their attention ahead to the New York Yankees. The American League Wild Card Series will begin on Tuesday, September 29th in the Bronx. First pitch is scheduled for 8:00 p.m. EST.
It’s Been a Career Season for Contreras
The frustrating part of the injuries for Contreras, other than that it could cost him time in the postseason, is that this has been a career season for him. This comes in his first year with the Red Sox as he’s brought a swing made for Fenway Park to Boston.
He’s hitting .276 with a .905 OPS. Contreras also has 27 home runs and 81 RBIs. That’s in a 129 game effort, and amounted to 4.5 WAR, per Baseball Reference.
Statistically, it’s Contreras’ best season. His previous high for WAR was 4.2 back in 2021. Otherwise, he hadn’t cracked that 4.0 WAR mark before. That was also a new single-season high for home runs and RBIs in his career. So, maybe it shouldn’t be a surprise that’s a career-record for OPS in a season, too.
The Red Sox need that version of Contreras in the postseason. Without him, they’re going to be looking far and wide for their power in the lineup.

item.dc:creator: Mac Cerullo

item.content:encoded:
Willson Contreras is back in the lineup for the final game of the regular season, but the Red Sox got some bad injury news on the eve of the playoffs.
Tyron Guerrero, one of the club’s top set-up man, has been placed on the 15-day injured list with a right shoulder strain. He won’t be eligible to return until Oct. 9, which means he will be sidelined through at least the American League Divisional Series.
The Red Sox also placed catcher Mickey Gasper on the 10-day IL with a right biceps strain, transferred outfielder Eli White to the 60-day IL, optioned right-hander Jedixson Paez, called up outfielder Nate Eaton and right-hander Wyatt Olds and activated right-hander Tanner Houck, who will start Sunday’s finale at Tropicana Field against the Chicago Cubs after missing the entire season recovering from Tommy John surgery.
Guerrero was only recently activated from the IL after missing 17 games with right shoulder inflammation. He was activated last Sunday and appeared in two games this past week, tossing one scoreless inning each against the Tampa Bay Rays last Sunday and against the Cleveland Guardians on Wednesday.
Evidently he suffered a setback, and with Justin Slaten also sidelined the Red Sox bullpen will enter October without two key set-up men behind Aroldis Chapman and Garrett Whitlock.
Contreras being back for the finale is, however, highly encouraging. The veteran slugger has been Boston’s best all-around hitter this season but hasn’t played since being hit on the right hand by a pitch on Sept. 17 against the Texas Rangers. He avoided a fracture but was unable to swing pain free for more than a week, and this past Thursday he expressed significant concern about his potential availability for the Wild Card Series.
Contreras will serve as the designated hitter on Sunday and will bat third.

item.title: [heavy.com] Red Sox Announce Surprise Decision on Starting Pitcher Before Cubs Season Finale
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Vankin
item.description: The Boston Red Sox made a surprise announcement before their season-ending game against the Chicago Cubs in Tampa Bay Sunday. Tanner Houck will take the mound for the Red Sox, starting the game and concluding an injury rehab that has stretched more than 16 months since his last big league pitch. The assignment came together late, a sign of how unsettled Boston’s roster still is, and it puts real pressure on an arm that hasn’t thrown a competitive pitch since Tommy John surgery sidelined him last
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox made a surprise announcement before their season-ending game against the Chicago Cubs in Tampa Bay Sunday. Tanner Houck will take the mound for the Red Sox, starting the game and concluding an injury rehab that has stretched more than 16 months since his last big league pitch.
The assignment came together late, a sign of how unsettled Boston’s roster still is, and it puts real pressure on an arm that hasn’t thrown a competitive pitch since Tommy John surgery sidelined him last year.
Game 162 was never supposed to happen in Florida. A forecasted nor’easter pushed the finale to Tropicana Field, according to theScore‘s Simon Sharkey-Gotlieb, sending both clubs to St. Petersburg right after Friday’s doubleheader at Fenway Park.
Boston is locked into the American League’s No. 5 seed and opens the Wild Card Series Tuesday at Yankee Stadium. The Cubs, already in the playoffs, send left-hander Shota Imanaga to the mound while they play out the string for seeding.
MLB.com’s own lineup page still listed Boston’s starter as TBD deep into Sunday morning, but beat reporters closed the gap first, with The Boston Globe’s Tim Healey and MassLive’s Chris Cotillo both confirming Houck’s assignment hours before first pitch.
| BOSTON RED SOX — ROSTER MOVES | |
|---|---|
| Move | Details |
| Recalled | Infielder/outfielder Nate Eaton and right-handed pitcher Wyatt Olds. |
| Reinstated | Right-handed pitcher Tanner Houck from the 60-Day Injured List; he will start today’s game against the Chicago Cubs. |
| Placed on IL | Catcher/first baseman Mickey Gasper — 10-Day IL (retroactive to Sept. 26), right biceps strain. |
| Placed on IL | Right-handed pitcher Tyron Guerrero — 15-Day IL (retroactive to Sept. 24), right shoulder strain. |
| Transferred | Outfielder Eli White to the 60-Day Injured List. |
| Boston Red Sox roster moves, Fenway Park, Boston, MA. | |
Tanner Houck and the Boston Red Sox’s 16-Month Wait
Houck’s 2025 season came apart fast. He opened the year as Boston’s No. 2 starter behind Garrett Crochet, then posted an 8.04 ERA across nine outings, including two starts in which he allowed 11 earned runs apiece, against Tampa Bay and Detroit.
That Detroit start, a 14-2 loss in which he walked three and struck out none, stands as Houck’s last big league appearance before Sunday.
He landed on the injured list days later with a right flexor strain, and a rehab assignment that July got cut short by the same elbow. Tommy John surgery followed in August 2025, then a return to the 60-day injured list this past February wiped out his entire 2026 regular season.
Houck made his final tuneup Saturday, Sept. 19, for Triple-A Worcester, allowing two runs, one earned on a solo homer, over 3 1/3 relief innings, his fourth and last rehab outing.
“Long year, long process. But this was the goal from Day 1,” Houck said, recalling the target he set in spring, as quoted by MLB.com‘s Ian Browne.
Interim manager Chad Tracy has kept his read on Houck simple.
“Let’s see how these outings go and how he feels and go from there,” Tracy said, as quoted by MLB.com.

Boston Red Sox Weigh Tanner Houck for October
Houck, 30, was Boston’s first-round pick in 2017, No. 24 overall out of Missouri, debuted in September 2020 and is now the longest-tenured player on the Red Sox roster. He made the All-Star team in 2024, going 9-10 with a 3.12 ERA over 30 starts, and carries a career mark of 24-32 with a 3.97 ERA and 449 strikeouts across parts of seven seasons.
None of that guarantees him a Wild Card Series spot. According to a Just Baseball roster projection, however, Houck may beat out fellow rehabbing reliever Johan Oviedo for a bullpen job largely on the strength of his postseason experience.
The Boston Globe‘s Peter Abraham raised the same possibility last week, writing that Houck could factor into the Wild Card mix if his rehab wrapped up cleanly.
No official roster has been announced. Boston will make that call after tonight’s results, with Houck’s final piece of evidence sitting right in front of them.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Red Sox Have Secret Weapon to Unleash on Yankees Series
item.dc:creator: Patrick McAvoy; Unknown
item.description: The Boston Red Sox have just one more regular season game left to be played in 2026 on Sunday before a wild-card series against the New York Yankees will kick off on Tuesday at Yankee Stadium. Beforehand, the Red Sox should find a way to get Romy Gonzalez on the playoff roster. The easiest way to do so would be to replace Andruw Monasterio with Gonzalez. Now, this isn't to say that Monasterio hasn't been a solid depth piece for Boston this season. He has been. But Gonzalez has been red-hot at th
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox have just one more regular season game left to be played in 2026 on Sunday before a wild-card series against the New York Yankees will kick off on Tuesday at Yankee Stadium.
Beforehand, the Red Sox should find a way to get Romy Gonzalez on the playoff roster. The easiest way to do so would be to replace Andruw Monasterio with Gonzalez. Now, this isn't to say that Monasterio hasn't been a solid depth piece for Boston this season. He has been. But Gonzalez has been red-hot at the plate down in Triple-A, has helped to carry the load at first base last season and has specifically had success against Max Fried, who is expected to be the Yankees' Game 1 starter, per USA Today's Bob Nightengale.
Red Sox fans know what Gonzalez can do. This is a guy who absolutely crushes lefties. It's why he had such a large role in 2025. He began the 2026 season on the Injured List and then struggled in 19 games after being promoted. But at the time he was activated, the Red Sox's offense was thin and arguably too much was asked of Gonzalez right away. He hasn't played in a big league game since July 29 after being demoted. He's been down in Triple-A and has been crushing. Since Aug. 25, Gonzalez has slashed .388/.456/.633 with a 1.089 OPS, two home runs, 13 RBIs, seven walks, six doubles and eight runs scored. That should be enough to get a look in the playoffs.
The Red Sox Should Give Romy Gonzalez A Shot
But he's also had success against Fried. Gonzalez has faced the lefty a handful of times and is 2-for-7 with a triple and two walks.
In 2025, Gonzalez slashed .331/.378/.600 with a .978 OPS against lefties, to go along with seven homers and 25 RBIs.
Again, Fried is likely to take the hill for the Yankees in Game 1. Then, the righty Cam Schlittler would likely be on the mound in Game 2. If the Red Sox were to make it to a Game 3, the likely hurlers would be the lefty Carlos Rodón or the righty Gerrit Cole. The fact that the Yankees could roll with two elite lefties should be enough for the Red Sox to give Gonzalez a shot.
Especially, with Willson Contreras up in the air, the Red Sox should be stocking up on righty batters. Monasterio has been good this season, but he doesn't have the offensive upside that Gonzalez does. He has had success vs. lefties and is red-hot. He should be on Boston's playoff roster, despite not finishing the regular season in the majors.

item.title: [BoSox Injection] Roman Anthony’s breakout against Cubs could save the Red Sox at just the right time
item.dc:creator: Brandon Glick
item.description: With the second Wild Card locked up and a Nor'easter throwing the Boston Red Sox's schedule into flux this weekend, no one would have blamed the team if they took things easy while preparing for a trip to the Bronx to kick off their postseason run. Instead, they crushed the Chicago Cubs' hopes and dreams, sweeping a Friday doubleheader at Fenway before flying south for the regular season finale at Tropicana Field. Brilliant pitching was mostly responsible for that pair of momentum-sealing victor
item.content:encoded:
With the second Wild Card locked up and a Nor'easter throwing the Boston Red Sox's schedule into flux this weekend, no one would have blamed the team if they took things easy while preparing for a trip to the Bronx to kick off their postseason run. Instead, they crushed the Chicago Cubs' hopes and dreams, sweeping a Friday doubleheader at Fenway before flying south for the regular season finale at Tropicana Field.
Brilliant pitching was mostly responsible for that pair of momentum-sealing victories, holding the potent Cubs offense to just three runs over two games. But more positive than anything was Roman Anthony's performance — he looked as comfortable at the plate as he has all year during the doubleheader.
All told, he went 4-for-6 with two walks, three extra-base hits, and three runs, posting an enormous 436 wRC+ between both contests. Coming on the same day that Mickey Gasper was potentially lost for the season, Anthony's breakout must be a sign of what's to come in October if the Red Sox have any hope of avenging last year's Wild Card Round loss to the New York Yankees.
Red Sox's injured, struggling offense leaves the team's fate in Roman Anthony's hands
Since returning from injury in late August, it's no secret that Anthony has been mired in a rust-related slump. Prior to his dominant showing against the Cubs, he had posted just a 99 wRC+ in his first 102 plate appearances back, featuring an on-base percentage below .300.
That just isn't going to get it done, especially when the rest of the offense can't produce with any sort of consistency. Since Anthony returned to the fold on Aug. 30, the players with the highest wRC+ marks on the Red Sox are: Willson Contreras (156), Eli White (144), Anthony (123), and Gasper (118). Every single one of those players, save for the left fielder, is currently injured.
That includes Contreras, who isn't actually on the IL. However, he recently told reporters that his hand hurts too much to swing a bat, meaning that even if he did try to accelerate his return from a hit by pitch, his impact would likely be muted. Considering that he's been the single-most important hitter in the lineup by a country mile this season, his absence looms large.
A return to form from Anthony would go a long way toward mitigating that loss, especially since he's settled back into his everyday spot atop Chad Tracy's lineup. If the Red Sox's offense has any chance of surviving the postseason, they'll need their star leadoff hitter to keep playing like a star.

item.title: [roundtable.io] If Boston Red Sox Are Going to Have Postseason Success They Need Roman Anthony
item.dc:creator: Zach Coe

Entering the 2026 season, no player on the Boston Red Sox faced more pressure to perform than 22-year-old phenom Roman Anthony. After striking out on free-agent sluggers Pete Alonso and Kyle Schwarber, and watching Alex Bregman depart for the Chicago Cubs, the weight of the Boston offense rested firmly on the former top overall prospect’s shoulders. item.content:encoded:
Boston’s performance in the playoffs may hinge on the young phenom’s ability to deliver.
Entering the 2026 season, no player on the Boston Red Sox faced more pressure to perform than 22-year-old phenom Roman Anthony. After striking out on free-agent sluggers Pete Alonso and Kyle Schwarber, and watching Alex Bregman depart for the Chicago Cubs, the weight of the Boston offense rested firmly on the former top overall prospect’s shoulders.
An impressive, injury-shortened 2025 season, in which the then-21-year-old hit .292/.396/.463/.859 in 71 games, showed Anthony was more than capable of being THE GUY in a lineup. However, in a small sample size in 2026, that has proven to be a bit too ambitious.
In his first 30 games of the season, Anthony hit just .229/.354/.321/. 675, struggling to adapt to pitchers' adjustments, including throwing him more off-speed pitches than fastballs. Anthony had shown signs of breaking out at the plate in late April, but then he suffered a torn ligament in his right ring finger, an injury that kept him out for over three months.
When the 22-year-old phenom returned to the lineup on Aug. 30, he came out of the gate firing, hitting .455/.500/.909/1.409 with two home runs, two doubles, and a triple in his first five games. However, in his last 19 games, Anthony has struggled mightily, hitting just .215/.262/.367/.629 with two home runs, four doubles, and one triple.
Once again, though, Anthony has shown recent signs of breaking out in a big way at the plate, going 4-for-6 with two doubles and a triple in Friday's doubleheader against the Cubs.
Injuries starting to stack up
It will be even more important for the Red Sox to get their 22-year-old face of the franchise going at the plate given that the team has seen two massive pieces, Willson Contreras and Mickey Gasper, go down with injuries in recent weeks, putting their playoff status in jeopardy.
With Gasper almost certainly missing at least the Wild Card round and potentially the entire postseason, and Contreras' status in doubt thanks to what he described as a bone bruise, the pressure is on underperforming players like Anthony and Wilyer Abreu to step up. In Anthony's case, he needs set the table for the middle of the order, and in Abreu's case, he needs to start to cashing in those opportunities.
Up next for the Sox
Anthony will have one more opportunity in the regular season to build on Friday's strong showing as the Red Sox and Cubs escape a New England nor'easter and head to Tampa to complete their three-game series from Tropicana Field on Sunday. Neither team has named its starting pitcher for the series finale. First pitch is set for 3:05 p.m. ET.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Red Sox Seeing Roman Anthony Green Flag Just Before Playoffs
item.dc:creator: Patrick McAvoy; Unknown
item.description: The Boston Red Sox are just a few days away from kicking off a three-game wild-card series against the New York Yankees on the road for the second straight season. Boston and New York will begin the postseason run on Sep. 29. As the regular season has wrapped up, the biggest red flag for the Red Sox has been their sluggish offense. Throughout the month of September, Boston's offense has been one of the worst in the league. In fact, Boston has scored the fewest runs in baseball in September with
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox are just a few days away from kicking off a three-game wild-card series against the New York Yankees on the road for the second straight season.
Boston and New York will begin the postseason run on Sep. 29. As the regular season has wrapped up, the biggest red flag for the Red Sox has been their sluggish offense. Throughout the month of September, Boston's offense has been one of the worst in the league. In fact, Boston has scored the fewest runs in baseball in September with just 69 in 23 games. But there is a bright spot, Boston fans. Roman Anthony is starting to look like himself at the plate at the perfect time.
Since Sep. 18, Anthony has batted .357 (10-for-28) with one homer, four doubles and a triple in seven games played. That's the type of production that is going to get the offense back on track. With Willson Contreras up in the air with his hand sore after getting hit by a pitch and Mickey Gasper also getting hurt, Boston needs guys to step up right now. The lights are starting to get bright. Boston has just one more regular season game left on Sunday before the full focus will turn to the playoffs.
Roman Anthony Is Getting Hot
If the Red Sox are going to make a run, they're going to need a lot from Anthony. When healthy, the Red Sox have arguably the deepest lineup in the American League playoffs, but will they actually find a way to get healthy? That's the question. Again, Contreras is up in the air. Gasper hurt his bicep on Friday and the club didn't give an optimistic update in the aftermath. Curtis Mead is on the shelf right now, although he is working his way back. Ceddanne Rafaela missed some time. Masataka Yoshida is on the Injured List as well, and the list goes on and on.
Boston isn't entering the playoffs at full strength, so it needs the guys who are healthy to carry the load to give this club enough time to advance and get closer to full strength. There isn't a guy in the lineup who moves the needle more than Anthony when he's rolling. We've started to see signs of that. If you have Anthony consistently getting on base at the top of the order, there's still enough talent behind him to get some runs in.
Boston's biggest strength is the pitching. The rotation and bullpen have carried the load all season. If they keep pitching as they have, Boston won't need many runs to win games. If Anthony can keep up his recent hot streak, that could be enough to help push Boston forward. He's that impactful.

item.title: [BoSox Injection] Red Sox still haven’t ruled out last-minute activation in wake of devastating Willson Contreras news
item.dc:creator: Katie Manganelli
item.description: The Boston Red Sox on September 24 dodged a bullet with a second potential Ceddanne Rafaela injury, but got a devastating Willson Contreras update. The veteran is still feeling pain while swinging after he was hit on his right hand by a pitch and he called into question his availability for the postseason. The Red Sox also got an update on a long shot return candidate that could keep some hope alive. Trade deadline acquisition Curtis Mead on Friday will take batting practice off a pitching machi
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox on September 24 dodged a bullet with a second potential Ceddanne Rafaela injury, but got a devastating Willson Contreras update. The veteran is still feeling pain while swinging after he was hit on his right hand by a pitch and he called into question his availability for the postseason.
The Red Sox also got an update on a long shot return candidate that could keep some hope alive. Trade deadline acquisition Curtis Mead on Friday will take batting practice off a pitching machine, according to Tim Healey of The Boston Globe (subscription required).
Mead will head to Fort Myers to join a number of players the Red Sox already have there, and Garrett Crochet will join him. Healey reports that Mead might take more batting practice off Crochet on Saturday.
The Red Sox have not formally ruled out activating Mead before the Wild Card round, which begins on September 29. It will be a close call, but there is still a slight chance that Mead could join the team before the first playoff series.
There's still a slim chance Curtis Mead could be ready for Red Sox's Wild Card series
The Red Sox dealt for Mead at the trade deadline to bring some power to their infield. The second baseman slashed .254/.352/.500 with 17 doubles and 17 home runs with the Washington Nationals. He's been on the injured list healing a fractured wrist after two at-bats in a Red Sox uniform. He hasn't appeared in a game since July 27.
There is some risk to rushing Mead back into action since he hasn't played in so long. If he does return, he'll do so without a rehab assignment because the WooSox's season has been over since September 19. If Mead isn't properly warmed up, a postseason rotation will be a rude awakening.
Still, the Red Sox's offense needs a serious lift, and even the possibility that Mead could help might be motivation enough for them to add him to the playoff roster. Boston's bats have slumped hard in September — the Red Sox have the second-lowest batting average (.221) and OPS (.656) this month and they won't get past the New York Yankees' pitching staff in that state.
Red Sox fans shouldn't get their hopes up about Mead's return. Even though he hasn't been ruled out, any blip in his recovery could cause a delay he can't come back from. He's also not as warmed up as he would be if he was returning in the regular season with a chance to go on a rehab assignment.
But Boston is desperate for a spark. If there's even a chance Mead could bring it, the Sox should let him try.

item.content:encoded:
In a season that will be defined by impactful performances from unlikely sources, Mickey Gasper's rise was the most unbelievable of all.
Yet Gasper's story will not have a postseason, after he suffered a peculiar injury in the Red Sox' third-to-last game of the season.
In the bottom of the fifth inning on Friday afternoon, Gasper swung and missed on a curveball, immediately flexing and grabbing at his right arm on his way to the dugout. He was replaced by Connor Wong, and between games, reports indicated that Gasper's injury was serious.
After the nightcap, manager Chad Tracy confirmed that the injury does appear to be one that will make Gasper unavailable for the postseason.
"At this point, it just looks like a significant biceps injury. So, he's gonna still be seeing more doctors and stuff like that. We'll get a final conclusion, but it's a pretty significant biceps injury," Tracy said. "It's probably gonna take him out."
The 30-year-old Gasper had cooled off since his historic month of August but still figured to be a useful lefty bat for Tracy when the Red Sox take on the Yankees next week for a best-of-three series, beginning on Tuesday. Gasper was catching in Friday's matinee, which would have given Tracy more flexibility in various situations.
Gasper batted .251 with an .823 OPS in 67 games with the Red Sox this season, doing most of his damage in the month of August. That month, he batted .400 with a 1.671 OPS, belting nine extra-base hits in 30 at-bats.
Combined with Willson Contreras declaring himself unlikely to be able to play when the playoffs begin, the Red Sox' lineup has now taken serious hits on consecutive days.
The Yankees are dealing with some injuries, too, though Aaron Judge, Giancarlo Stanton and Trent Grisham are all working toward being able to return for the postseason.
